subject.title: fix(node): fail closed on invalid trusted-proxy CIDRs and warn on untrusted forwarding

question: Should malformed Node trusted-proxy CIDRs remain fail-safe-but-running for upgrade compatibility, or should all affected coordinators fail startup after upgrading?
rationale: The former preserves availability while ignoring unsafe forwarding data; the latter makes configuration errors unmistakable but can turn a previously running deployment into a total outage. Repository behavior does not establish which tradeoff maintainers intend.

options.title: Compatibility-Safe Default
options.body: Continue treating malformed entries as untrusted, emit an actionable diagnostic, and add an explicit strict-startup option for operators who want rejection.

options.title: Unconditional Startup Rejection
options.body: Retain the proposed failure behavior, document the upgrade impact, and require live upgrade and recovery evidence before merge.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Land the rate-limited warning while deferring startup strictness until the compatibility policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Compatibility-Safe Default
recommendation.body: Continue treating malformed entries as untrusted, emit an actionable diagnostic, and add an explicit strict-startup option for operators who want rejection.
